subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Oxidation is best defined as:
questions.explain: Remember OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain (of electrons).

questions.q: Reduction is:
questions.explain: Reduction is the gain of electrons (and often a decrease in oxidation number).

questions.q: In a redox reaction, the oxidising agent is the species that:
questions.explain: The oxidising agent oxidises another species by accepting its electrons, so it is reduced.

questions.q: The oxidation number of an uncombined element such as O2 or Na is:
questions.explain: Elements in their standard state have an oxidation number of zero.

questions.q: The oxidation number of sulfur in the sulfate ion SO4^2- is:
questions.explain: Oxygen is -2 (four give -8); overall charge -2 means sulfur is +6.

questions.q: In the reaction Zn + Cu2+ → Zn2+ + Cu, zinc is:
questions.explain: Zinc loses electrons (0 to +2), so it is oxidised and acts as the reducing agent.

questions.q: A reducing agent is a species that:
options: Donates electrons and is itself oxidised
questions.explain: The reducing agent reduces another species by giving up electrons, so it is oxidised.

questions.q: The half-equation for the reduction of copper(II) ions is:
questions.explain: Reduction gains electrons, converting Cu2+ to Cu.

questions.q: In a metal displacement reaction, a more reactive metal will:
options: Displace a less reactive metal from its salt solution
Be displaced by a less reactive metal
questions.explain: A more reactive metal reduces the less reactive metal ion, e.g. Zn displaces Cu from CuSO4.

questions.q: When the oxidation number of an element increases during a reaction, the element has been:
questions.explain: An increase in oxidation number corresponds to loss of electrons (oxidation).

questions.q: The oxidation number of hydrogen in most compounds (e.g. HCl, H2O) is:
questions.explain: Hydrogen is usually +1, except in metal hydrides where it is -1.

questions.q: The oxidation number of manganese in MnO4- (permanganate) is:
questions.explain: Four oxygens give -8; overall -1 means manganese is +7.

questions.q: A disproportionation reaction is one in which a single species is:
questions.explain: In disproportionation the same element is simultaneously oxidised and reduced.

questions.q: In the reaction 2Na + Cl2 → 2NaCl, chlorine is:
questions.explain: Chlorine goes from 0 to -1, gaining electrons, so it is reduced and is the oxidising agent.

questions.q: In the reactivity series, a metal higher up is:
options: More easily oxidised (a stronger reducing agent)
questions.explain: More reactive metals lose electrons more readily and displace less reactive metals.

questions.q: When iron rusts, the iron is:
questions.explain: Rusting is the oxidation of iron in the presence of oxygen and water.

questions.q: In balancing redox half-equations, electrons are added to:
questions.explain: Electrons are added to one side so that the total charge is equal on both sides.

questions.q: Acidified potassium manganate(VII) is often used as an oxidising agent because it is:
options: Readily reduced, turning from purple to colourless
questions.explain: MnO4- (purple) is reduced to Mn2+ (colourless), a useful self-indicating redox titration.

questions.q: The oxidation number of oxygen in hydrogen peroxide H2O2 is unusually:
questions.explain: In peroxides oxygen is -1 rather than its usual -2.

questions.q: Overall, a redox reaction always involves:
options: Transfer of electrons from the reducing agent to the oxidising agent
questions.explain: Oxidation and reduction always occur together, coupling electron loss and gain.
